name: Leon White
life: “I still remember mending a crate while two owners argued about the rent.” Monday often includes a stop at the window at Night Shift Donuts, where Leon knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I used the berth for pocket money and never asked whose money repaired it.
appearance: Leon is easy to recognize by a thin scattering of white hair over the crown and two dimples that appear only with a full smile. Usually dressed in a plum-colored cardigan with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve, Leon turns fully toward the person speaking when listening.
personality: Leon finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
agenda: To establish who paid for the old repairs.
family: Mara Tev is Leon’s cousin. Leon chooses the music. Mara puts the kettle on. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *The last green*, Mara says, “His callsign has been on my board since I joined.”
connections: Sasha Watts. A berth used for pocket money belongs to a family whose photographs omitted a member.

reactions.situation: A relative wants the absent signer's address
reactions.response: Leon asks the absent person what address, if any, can be shared.

reactions.situation: Someone begins blaming the youngest worker for a missing item
reactions.response: Leon brings the worker into the conversation and asks what they remember without feeding them a story.

reactions.situation: When somebody waves from across traffic
reactions.response: Leon waits at the corner to hear their voice and give them a proper answer.
